answer.rationale: Rollback is ruled out by the compliance constraint. Regional failover is best suited to localized degradation, and this is a system-wide write-path latency climb during peak settlement, making it riskier. Enabling a circuit breaker could shed needed writes and violate the objective of preserving customer writes. Routing to read replicas addresses read load, not the degraded write path. Adding capacity is the only intervention that directly relieves write-path pressure while preserving all customer writes and keeping the mandatory security patch in place. It is also consistent with inherited memory of headroom absorbing surges without queue degradation.
